variants.headline: Building finished and handed over
variants.sub: The project {project} has been completed and handed over by {builder}.
variants.body:
The builder {builder} has finished and handed over {project}. It opens next month. The distinction between handover and opening matters to an assessment of {target}: a building has been delivered, while its entry into use is the following stage rather than an event already accomplished by this notice.

The gazette records construction and handover as completed. The gazette records the development as a matter deserving careful attention in the public interest.

variants.headline: Delivery reached; opening follows
variants.sub: Completion and handover of {project} have been achieved by {builder}.
variants.body:
The project {project} has been completed and handed over by {builder}, with opening next month. The delivery is a practical result rather than merely an intention to build. Readers considering {target} should recognise that result while keeping the beginning of operations distinct from the completion of construction.

The gazette records construction and handover as completed. The gazette records the development as a matter deserving careful attention in the public interest.

variants.headline: A completed project leaves the builder's hands
variants.sub: The builder {builder} has finished and handed over {project}.
variants.body:
Completion and handover have been reached for {project}, built by {builder}. Opening follows next month. For {target}, the event provides a concrete point at which delivery can be judged, without turning a finished building into a claim about results that its later use has not yet established.

The gazette records construction and handover as completed. The gazette records the development as a matter deserving careful attention in the public interest.
